palette.notes: No clip shows the original SNES art (clip1 instrument cover, clip2 dance video, clip3 fan HD-remake reimagining), so palette facts stay from the wiki: one colour world per era; Toriyama's flat bright heroes on richer backgrounds. The fan clip keeps one dominant hue per location.

lighting: From the wiki: ambient, era-wide mood lighting; the graphics lead cited the film Alien, so dark interiors and ruined future maps lean dim and cool while heroes stay bright. The fan clip's god rays and rim-lit heroes are not the original look.
silhouette: Toriyama's chunky proportions (big heads, distinct hair: Crono's red spikes, Frog's shape, Robo's round body) keep each hero readable at sprite size; the fan clip's portrait cards still read from hair spike and body block alone.

motion.timing: No metrics file and no original footage in the clips: describe only. Per the wiki and the game's reputation: a short reusable pose set (walk, run, nod, head-shake, surprised jump, laugh, collapse) cut together on held beats rather than long tweens.

texture: From the wiki: tile-built maps with soft dithered shading on rocks, trees and floors; characters cleaner and flatter than the ground. The fan clip pushes background density (cables, crates, foliage) far beyond the original while keeping the party as tiny clean sprites.
camera: Fixed top-down 3/4 view; scenes scroll to frame the action instead of cutting. The fan clip keeps a wide 3/4 establishing frame per location and cuts between places every ~7 s with a black-background quote card in between.

acting.enters: Walk or run in from screen edges and doorways on the same map; enemies are visible on the field before a fight. The fan clip walks the party in single file along a path into each set.
acting.acts: A handful of poses (nod, head-shake, surprise jump, laugh, faint) do all the emotion; NPCs talk while the player can still move.
acting.exits: Walk off-screen or through a door; fights start and end on the same map with no black transition screen.
acting.depth: Tiny party sprites low in a huge set (portal plaza, market street, castle town) so the world dwarfs them; the field battle keeps the world visible behind the fight.

techniques: small reusable pose library cut together on held beats
battles staged on the field map, no separate battle screen
readable hero silhouette from exaggerated proportions (hair spike, big head)
one dominant hue per era/location so place reads before story
background-level dithering, flatter characters on top
tiny party in a large set to sell scale
feel: per-era colour world + flat bright heroes + 6-pose acting library = expressive tiny actors that never leave the stage
for_fred: Give Fred a small pose library (nod, head-shake, surprise hop, laugh) and cut between them on the narration beats instead of looping one animation. Keep the scene continuous: Fred swims off the edge, the frame holds, he comes back from another side; once, show him tiny in a big set to sell scale.
